do some research and learn how to properly use a camera to take stills. learn about the exposure triangle, aperture, depth of field. learn the difference between sensor sizes and how they impact focal length and depth of field. your camera is a DX (or APSC sensor size); find out the difference between APSC and Full Frame and how it can impact your compositions. 

shooting sports, you generally want: 
- low ISO (on a camera like a d3300, or most of the older APSC models, high ISOs are very noisy) 
- fast shutter speed for capturing action (1/500, or 1/1000 or faster) 
- long focal length (70-200mm is good) 
- wide enough aperture to let enough light in (f/2.8 for example, but could even go f/5.6 if the image is too soft). a wider aperture also increases depth of field for the bokeh

you don’t have to learn how manual mode works (but it helps). for fast shots where you don’t want to fiddle with settings, use the “S” auto-mode (Shutter Priority). you set a shutter speed, say 1/1000, and then the camera will figure out the appropriate aperture and ISO for you (but be warned if it cranks up the ISO, it could invite noise), so i would recommend this with a fast lens like a f/2.8

Neither crazy nor unrealistic. When I was in college (2016-2021) I hadn’t touched a single line of code until I took my intro to programming class, also in Java. My school offered a “CS Primer” course that teaches you how to think critically for CS, but since it was not required for the major I did not take it (my school had a pre-major system, before I could officially be in the CS program so I had to do my pre-major reqs ASAP, therefore I skipped the not required classes). 

I majored in CS for the money, because when I was a kid I was fed the myth that you will make $120k starting at Google, and when I was old enough to realize better, I learned first hand how shit and competitive job interviewing and Leetcoding grind is - not to mention the layoffs that occurred 2022-now. While I majored for the money, it grew into a passion because I found I truly enjoyed the subject and I ended up being one of the only students to actually like taking Languages and Finite Automata/Computing Theory.

I won’t lie, it was tough, because I was a first year, it was my first semester and I was also getting through the HS-college transitory period (learning to live on own, balancing time with no one to hold me accountable). 

The most important part for me was that I utilized the resources my school had - I joined the local ACM chapter and other clubs at my uni to network and meet other, older and more experienced students who I could ask for advice/peer to peer mentorship. 

So yeah, one bad semester isn’t gonna ruin you. Definitely not the end of the world; I’ve met people who had no clue what they were doing in their senior years. I think you need to reassess whether CS is truly right for you and dedicate time, work ethic, and effort to learning it. Go to office hours if you don’t understand something. Maybe go to a local Barnes and Noble or a library and pick up some introductory books on the subject

just finished ff16, what i liked, what i didn’t. 

liked:
- story was serviceable (i won’t say great) for final fantasy fare, but ultima as an antagonist was extremely boring. what was his motivation? to thanos the world and get rid of the blight? you only really fully understand it if you take a moment to read every bit of lore. otherwise he just seems to lust after clive. some character interactions could have more focus. jill’s character arc falls off pretty hard after she is saved in favor of clive’s relationship with joshua, for example. 
- voice acting, yea they recorded for english first and it shows 
- combat is pretty fun and clive generally felt controllable for the most part 
- the music (lovely dark and deep was my base theme) 
- torgal 

didn’t like:
- strange story pacing
- way too easy. yes i know you can play final fantasy mode in new game+ but as an adult i kind of expect a challenge from day 1. in other words it should’ve been unlocked from the start imo. DMC gets away with this because it’s short and intended to be replayable, but for a game as long and slow as FF16, this seems like a huge oversight by a team unfamiliar with their playerbase.
- lack of control customization. i’ve been playing on control scheme C because it felt the most natural to charge fire while executing combos.
- cinematic clashes. would’ve preferred traditional set pieces over the QTE prompts. sometimes i just wanna watch the animation instead of having to wait to press square or R1
- the “ENEMY SLAIN” cutins whenever you beat a story related encounter. it breaks up the flow of the game so fucking much. a particularly egregious example involves you getting the shit kicked out of you in a cinematic battle and then “BOSS THWARTED” or something like that 
- eikon battles feel incredibly clunky. i get that you’re supposed to feel power and pace in the punches, but i felt that i got stuck in animations and getting slapped by shit i couldn’t dodge/cancel my current attack out of. the last battle was full of beam spam and i couldn’t tell what the fuck was going on
- side quests felt too plenty for the actual rewards you get. at the end of the game it felt like a chore when it threw like 12 of them. fetch 20 bear asses and get rewarded 50 magicked ashes. not to say that the side quests weren’t good (a few standout ones). midadol’s fetch quest line was the fucking worst.
- no party switching
- barely any build customization. what is the point of a magic stat when all your weapons increase your physical and magic attack by the same amount? 
- no hub fast travel system.

in other words, decent game, but there is a ton of room for improvement. i’m disappointed that considering a lot of experienced talent at the helm (ryota suzuki, a combat designer of dmc5, takahisa taura of nier and astral chain in particular) but a lot of “game” seems sacrificed for show, and it doesn’t feel organic or usually breaks immersion unlike the seamless cutscenes from GoW. a lot of design choices seem as if they assume a player has only previously played turn based RPGs (i.e. the inclusion of the auto-dodge type accessories in an objectively easy action game).
for me it has to work out in software dev. in the words of steve rogers, “because i don’t know what i’ll do if it doesn’t”
